messages.content:
You answer a question about machines at work (law, guidance, manufacturers' manuals, company and plant
documents) using ONLY the numbered passages given. Each passage is headed by its document, its place and its rank.

Rules:
- Use only the passages. Do not use anything you know from elsewhere.
- Answer only if a passage states the answer for the exact subject asked about (the same device, the same article
  and paragraph, the same kind of verification, the same deadline). A passage about a neighbouring subject does not
  answer the question: then the kind is "unknown" and the value is null. A question about something that happened
  (the date of the last check, whether something is overdue today) is "unknown" unless a passage records that event.
- A passage marked "corrected by the corrigendum" already shows the corrected wording: reason with it. The old
  wording, given in the mark, is no longer valid.
- If the question asks about a day, compare that day with every date in the passages, one by one. A repeal or an
  application "from" a date takes effect on that date, not earlier: an act repealed from a date is still fully in
  force on every earlier day; a rule applying from a date does not yet bind on earlier days.
- When passages of different rank disagree, the higher rank wins: law, then guidance, then manufacturer's manual,
  then company procedure, then plant record. Between two Italian texts, a legislative decree (D.Lgs.) wins over a
  ministerial decree (DM). Say which one wins.
- A row of a table belongs to the thing named in that same row. Read the row of the item asked about, not a
  neighbouring row. When the question itself states a condition ("if it were in regular use", "built in 2017"),
  reason with that condition.
- The kind follows the question: "from which date / by which date / when (a day)" is "date"; "how often / for how
  long / within what time" is "duration"; "can / may / is / does / must" is "boolean"; "which / what (several
  things)" is "set"; who, why, under which condition is "text" (one short sentence naming every element asked for).
- Point at the evidence: for every passage you rely on, copy word for word the sentence, or the table row, that
  states what you use. Copy exactly, without changing a character; do not join text from two places.
- Return JSON only, with the reasoning first:
  {"reasoning": "what the passages say and how it leads to the answer, in a few short sentences",
   "kind": "set|date|duration|boolean|text|unknown",
   "value": <list of short strings for set | "YYYY-MM-DD" for date | ISO 8601 duration like "P10Y", "P6M", "P45D", "PT1H" | true/false | a short text | null>,
   "text": "one or two sentences for a person, naming the document and the article, section or page",
   "evidence": [{"passage": <number>, "quote": "<copied exactly from that passage>"}]}

Today is 2026-11-14.
Question: On 1 March 2027 a manufacturer places a vehicle servicing lift on the market. Among which conformity assessment procedures may it choose?

Passages:
[0] eu-dir-2014-33, Art. 16(1) — rank: law
Article 16 Conformity assessment procedures for lifts. 1. Lifts shall be subject to one of the following conformity assessment procedures: (a) if they are designed and manufactured in accordance with a model lift that has undergone an EU-type examination set out in in Annex IV, Part B: (i) final inspection for lifts set out in Annex V; (ii) conformity to type based on product quality assurance for lifts set out in Annex X; (iii) conformity to type based on production quality assurance for lifts set out in Annex XII; (b) if they are designed and manufactured under a quality system approved in accordance with Annex XI: (i) final inspection for lifts set out in Annex V; (ii) conformity to type based on product quality assurance for lifts set out in Annex X; (iii) conformity to type based on production quality assurance for lifts set out in Annex XII; (c) conformity based on unit verification for lifts set out in Annex VIII; (d) conformity based on full quality assurance plus design examination for lifts set out in Annex XI.

[1] eu-dir-2014-33, Recital 21 — rank: law
(21) In order to enable economic operators to demonstrate and the competent authorities to ensure that lifts placed on the market and safety components for lifts made available on the market conform to the essential health and safety requirements, it is necessary to provide for conformity assessment procedures. Decision No 768/2008/EC establishes modules for conformity assessment procedures, which include procedures from the least to the most stringent, in proportion to the level of risk involved and the level of safety required. In order to ensure inter-sectoral coherence and to avoid ad-hoc variants, conformity assessment procedures should be chosen from among those modules.

[2] eu-dir-2014-33, Art. 15 — rank: law
Article 15 Conformity assessment procedures for safety components for lifts Safety components for lifts shall be subject to one of the following conformity assessment procedures: (a) the model of the safety component for lifts shall be submitted for EU type examination set out in Annex IV, Part A and the conformity to type shall be ensured with random checking of the safety component for lifts set out in Annex IX; (b) the model of the safety component for lifts shall be submitted for EU type examination set out in Annex IV, Part A and be subject to conformity to type based on product quality assurance in accordance with Annex VI; (c) conformity based on full quality assurance set out in Annex VII.

[3] eu-dir-2014-68, Art. 14(3) — rank: law
Article 14 Conformity assessment procedures. 3. Pressure equipment shall be subject to one of the conformity assessment procedures which may be chosen by the manufacturer among those laid down for the category in which it is classified. The manufacturer may also choose to apply one of the procedures which apply to a higher category, if available.

[4] eu-dir-2014-33, Annex VII — rank: law
ANNEX VII CONFORMITY BASED ON FULL QUALITY ASSURANCE FOR SAFETY COMPONENTS FOR LIFTS (module H) 1. Conformity based on full quality assurance for safety components for lifts is the conformity assessment procedure whereby a notified body assesses the quality system of a manufacturer to ensure that the safety components for lifts are designed, manufactured, inspected and tested in order to satisfy the applicable requirements of Annex I and to enable a lift to which they are correctly incorporated to satisfy those requirements.

[5] eu-dir-2014-33, Annex XI — rank: law
ANNEX XI CONFORMITY BASED ON FULL QUALITY ASSURANCE PLUS DESIGN EXAMINATION FOR LIFTS (module H1) 1. Conformity based on full quality assurance plus design examination for lifts is the conformity assessment procedure whereby a notified body assesses the quality system of an installer and, where appropriate, the design of the lifts, to ensure that the lifts satisfy the applicable essential health and safety requirements set out in Annex I.

[6] eu-dir-2014-33, Art. 8(2) — rank: law
Article 8 Obligations of manufacturers. 2. Manufacturers shall draw up the required technical documentation and carry out the relevant conformity assessment procedure referred to in Article 15 or have it carried out Where compliance of a safety component for lifts with the applicable essential health and safety requirements has been demonstrated by that procedure, manufacturers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity, ensure that it accompanies the safety component for lifts and affix the CE marking.

[7] eu-dir-2014-33, Art. 10(2) — rank: law
Article 10 Obligations of importers. 2. Before placing a safety component for lifts on the market, importers shall ensure that the appropriate conformity assessment procedure referred to in Article 15 has been carried out by the manufacturer. They shall ensure that the manufacturer has drawn up the technical documentation, that the safety component for lifts bears the CE marking and is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity and the required documents, and that the manufacturer has complied with the requirements set out in Article 8(5) and (6). Where an importer considers or has reason to believe that a safety component for lifts is not in conformity with Article 5(2), he shall not place the safety component for lifts on the market until it has been brought into conformity. Furthermore, where the safety component for lifts presents a risk, the importer shall inform the manufacturer and the market surveillance authorities to that effect.

[8] eu-dir-2014-33, Recital 12 — rank: law
(12) It is necessary to ensure that safety components for lifts from third countries entering the Union market comply with this Directive, and in particular that the appropriate conformity assessment procedures have been carried out by the manufacturer with regard to those safety components for lifts. Provision should therefore be made for importers to make sure that the safety components for lifts they place on the market comply with the requirements of this Directive and that they do not place on the market safety components for lifts which do not comply with such requirements or present a risk. Provision should also be made for importers to make sure that conformity assessment procedures have been carried out and that marking of safety components for lifts and documentation drawn up by manufacturers are available for inspection by the competent national authorities.

[9] eu-dir-2014-33, Annex VII, 2 — rank: law
2. Obligations of the manufacturer The manufacturer shall operate an approved quality system for the design, manufacture, final inspection and testing of safety components for lifts as specified in point 3 and shall be subject to surveillance as specified in point 4.

[10] eu-dir-2014-33, Annex V — rank: law
ANNEX V FINAL INSPECTION FOR LIFTS 1. Final inspection is the part of a conformity assessment procedure whereby a notified body ascertains and certifies that a lift subject to an EU-type examination certificate or designed and manufactured according to an approved quality system satisfies the essential health and safety requirements set out in Annex I.

[11] REG, Annex III, 4.1.3 — rank: law
4.1.3. Fitness for purpose When lifting machinery or related products, including lifting accessories, are placed on the market or are first put into service, the manufacturer shall ensure, by taking appropriate measures or having them taken, that the machinery or related products, including lifting accessories, which are ready for use – whether manually or power-operated – can fulfil their specified functions safely. The static and dynamic tests referred to in section 4.1.2.3 shall be performed on all lifting machinery or related products ready to be put into service. Where the machinery or related products cannot be assembled in the manufacturer’s premises, the appropriate measures shall be taken at the place of use by the manufacturer. Otherwise, the measures may be taken either in the manufacturer’s premises or at the place of use.

response.text: {"reasoning": "Passage 0 (Art. 16(1) of Directive 2014/33/EU) lists the conformity assessment procedures for lifts: EU-type examination followed by Annex V, X or XII; a quality system approved under Annex XI followed by Annex V, X or XII; unit verification under Annex VIII; or full quality assurance plus design examination under Annex XI. No passage gives an application or repeal date for this Directive, so nothing indicates that it does not apply on 1 March 2027. The passages do not say whether vehicle servicing lifts are within scope, so the answer assumes they are lifts under Art. 16.","kind": "set","value": ["EU-type examination (Annex IV Part B) followed by final inspection (Annex V)","EU-type examination (Annex IV Part B) followed by conformity to type based on product quality assurance (Annex X)","EU-type examination (Annex IV Part B) followed by conformity to type based on production quality assurance (Annex XII)","design and manufacture under an approved quality system (Annex XI) followed by final inspection (Annex V)","design and manufacture under an approved quality system (Annex XI) followed by conformity to type based on product quality assurance (Annex X)","design and manufacture under an approved quality system (Annex XI) followed by conformity to type based on production quality assurance (Annex XII)","conformity based on unit verification (Annex VIII)","conformity based on full quality assurance plus design examination (Annex XI)"],"text": "Under Article 16(1) of Directive 2014/33/EU, a lift may follow one of the listed procedures, with the choice between EU-type examination routes, approved quality system routes, unit verification (Annex VIII) and full quality assurance plus design examination (Annex XI); the passages do not confirm whether vehicle servicing lifts are in scope.","evidence": [{"passage": 0, "quote": "Lifts shall be subject to one of the following conformity assessment procedures"}, {"passage": 0, "quote": "(c) conformity based on unit verification for lifts set out in Annex VIII"}, {"passage": 0, "quote": "(d) conformity based on full quality assurance plus design examination for lifts set out in Annex XI"}]}
